To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
inflation is a bad thing for growth, even if the latter is measured as a growth rate.
the negative correlation among GDP growth and inflation is robust to improvements in the empirical model, and that the estimated costs of high inflation are significant.

a) inflation does not seem to be a necessary condition for growth; b) inflation has a significant negative impact on growth; c) this impact is still significant once country-­specific effects are allowed for; and d) this impact is not explained by reverse causation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether there is an inverse relationship between inflation and growth.
the relationship between economic growth and inflation, and the costs of inflation.
the question whether the costs of inflation are a serious obstacle to economic growth.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
inflation is a negative determinant of economic growth.
the evidence on a negative relationship between growth and inflation is robust, but it is not strong.
, in the OECD area, inflation does harm growth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the evidence for the existence of a negative relation among growth and inflation, at the OECD level and over the period considered, withstands a number or improvements in the empirical specification of the model, which address the most common criticisms on this evidence.
the negative correlation between inflation and growth is robust to a number of improvements of the empirical model.
the negative correlation among GDP growth and inflation is robust to the most common econometric improvements.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the empirical relationship between inflation and growth is robust to several econometric improvements.
inflation is not a neutral phenomenon and that it does have an impact on the economy, even if the estimated costs of high inflation are not as large as the ones reported in the literature.
, while the negative correlation between inflation and growth is still significant in the data, it cannot be taken as an indication of the costs of inflation.
